verdict.summary: Core Scientific now has a visible colocation business rather than merely a mining conversion story. Q2 2026 revenue rose to $164.2 million from $78.6 million, colocation contributed $136.7 million, gross profit reached $70 million and non-GAAP adjusted EBITDA was $41.1 million. Billing capacity was 395 MW in Q2 and 437 MW by mid-July, supporting an annualized colocation GAAP revenue run rate near $635 million. The AMD partnership adds a 530 MW, 15-year anchor with more than $14 billion of potential base contract value, taking total leased power to 1.1 GW. The contradiction is cash intensity: Q2 capex was $797.5 million, trailing EBITDA remains negative in the point-in-time bundle, and the $1.155 billion GAAP net loss was distorted by fair-value changes on pre-existing warrants. An August facility added a $100 million revolver and $500 million letter-of-credit line with a $150 million liquidity floor but no new warrants. The C+ grade recognizes operating conversion but not yet mature returns. Trade status remains watch above $17.45.
whyBuy: Q2 revenue was $164.2M versus $78.6M a year earlier.
Colocation revenue reached $136.7M and gross profit $70M.
Billing capacity reached 437 MW by mid-July.
Total leased power reached 1.1 GW with more than $24B potential base value.
whyAvoid: Q2 GAAP net loss was $1.155B, heavily affected by warrant fair value.
The point-in-time bundle still shows negative trailing EBITDA.
The August credit package imposes a $150M minimum-liquidity covenant.
Two warrant classes tied to financing create additional per-share complexity.

business.overview:
Core Scientific develops high-density datacenters and sells colocation capacity under long-term contracts, while retaining a smaller digital-asset mining operation. Revenue is driven by billable megawatts, contractual pricing, power pass-throughs, uptime and residual mining hash economics.

The AI transmission channel is direct: customers such as CoreWeave and AMD reserve power and datacenter infrastructure, Core Scientific funds the conversion and build, and contracted fees begin as capacity is delivered. Billing power of 437 MW in mid-July versus 1.1 GW leased quantifies the remaining conversion runway.

The model breaks if construction is late, customer credit weakens, equipment or grid delivery fails, or financing covenants constrain the build. Potential contract value above $24B is undiscounted and delivered over many years. Warrant accounting can obscure operating results, while actual capex and liquidity determine whether common shareholders capture the residual economics. Investors should therefore track billing megawatts, customer acceptance, incremental rent and remaining construction cost together, rather than valuing the entire leased pipeline at an undiscounted contract headline.
business.moat: Core Scientific controls large powered campuses and has already demonstrated conversion from mining to billable HPC colocation. Its edge is speed-to-power and signed counterparties, but it remains capital-dependent and cannot rely on contract value alone to defend returns.

earnings.beatNote: Q2 2026 revenue was $164.2M versus $78.6M, with colocation revenue of $136.7M versus $10.6M. Gross profit increased to $70M from $5M, and non-GAAP adjusted EBITDA reached $41.1M versus $28.5M. GAAP net loss was $1.155B, primarily reflecting non-cash warrant fair-value movements rather than operating cash burn. Billing capacity was 395 MW in Q2 and 437 MW by mid-July, equivalent to approximately $635M of annualized colocation GAAP revenue. Core Scientific reported billing-run-rate milestones but no formal consolidated revenue or EBITDA guidance. The caveat is investment intensity: Q2 capex was $797.5M, and the 530 MW AMD build must be financed and delivered before its potential value is earned. No confirmed Core Scientific next-results date was shown in the official investor calendar reviewed.

capitalStructure.shareHistory: Core Scientific's June filing used 325.3M weighted-average basic shares and listed 182.7M potentially dilutive shares excluded from EPS: 69.6M from converts, 16.4M awards, 0.3M options and 96.4M Tranche 1 warrants. That produces an approximately 508.0M minimum observable diluted pro-forma denominator, 56.2% above basic; 6.6M penny-warrant shares were already included in basic EPS. The August $100M revolver and $500M letter-of-credit facility had no amount drawn at closing and issued no new warrants. The two listed warrant classes are 2024 restructuring securities, not financing-linked August instruments.

filingsReview.summary: 3 decision-relevant primary filing(s) are displayed with accession-specific findings. Grade C+ measures fundamentals; trade state watch measures timing and is evaluated separately.

filings.finding: The June Form 10-Q reports Q2 revenue of $164.2M, colocation revenue of $136.7M, project spending and warrant accounting, establishing current operating and liquidity risk. This classification controls the editorial conclusion.
The amended 2025 Form 10-K establishes Core Scientific's annual controls, warrants, debt and post-reorganization baseline; it predates the Q2 AMD lease and August credit facilities.

The August Form 8-K documents an undrawn-at-closing $100M secured revolver and $500M letter-of-credit facility plus a $150M liquidity floor. It creates debt and covenant capacity but discloses no new financing-linked warrant issuance; existing CORZW and CORZZ are pre-existing restructuring warrants.

contrarianRisks: The $600M August package is debt and letter-of-credit capacity, not common-equity issuance.
Two financing-linked warrant classes create dilution and fair-value volatility.
The $150M minimum-liquidity covenant reduces usable balance-sheet flexibility.
Potential contract value above $24B is undiscounted and conditional on delivery.
Quarterly capex of $797.5M materially exceeded current adjusted EBITDA.
